title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§48, 'Construction d'un schéma en groupes', in the 'équation des lacets' notes). Let G be a group scheme over a ring A; the examples are SL(2)_Z and GL(2)_Z. Let ρ ∈ G(A) be a section. The previous page defines the commutator morphism F_ρ: G → G, α ↦ [α,ρ] = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}. Let T_ρ = Centr_G(ρ). Then F_ρ(α') = F_ρ(α) exactly when α' ∈ αT_ρ. So F_ρ induces a monomorphism of fppf sheaves G/T_ρ ↪ G, and the problem is to describe its image.

The page gives three steps.

(i) First necessary condition (4): δ(ξ) = 1, where δ: G → G_ab is the canonical map to the abelianization (5). This holds because a commutator dies in G_ab. For SL2, G_ab is trivial, so the condition is empty; for GL2, G_ab = G_m via det, so the condition is det ξ = 1.

(ii) Second condition, which is tautologically necessary and sufficient: ξρ must be locally (fppf) conjugate to ρ. Indeed ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} if and only if ξρ = αρα^{-1}. This condition implies (4). Grothendieck notes that (4) can still serve as an ingredient in a computable ('calculatoire') necessary and sufficient criterion for ξρ ~ ρ.

(iii) For reductive G, local conjugacy is understood via Steinberg. There is a scheme of invariants I_G with a canonical morphism G → I_G (6). It is universal among conjugation-invariant morphisms from G to schemes, over A and compatibly with base change. So I_G is the 'representable envelope' of the fppf sheaf G/int(G) of conjugacy classes; in modern terms this is the adjoint (Chevalley–Steinberg) quotient G//G.

The next page completes the argument:
- The map G/int(G) → I_G is an fppf epimorphism but not a monomorphism.
- Equality of images in I_G is necessary for local conjugacy but not sufficient in general.
- It is sufficient when both sections are fibrewise regular in Steinberg's sense, or both are semisimple.
- For SL2 and GL2, regular means nowhere central, which holds for the ρ coming from Γ_∞ = Γ.

Consequence, implicit here: for SL2 and ρ nowhere central, the image of G/T_ρ → G is the closed subscheme {ξ : tr(ξρ) = tr(ρ)}. For GL2 one adds det ξ = 1. The purpose is to identify the solution set of a commutator ('loop') equation with a homogeneous space, giving a concrete scheme-theoretic model for the construction of the group scheme of §48.
errors: The condition is labelled Δ(ξ)=1 in (4) on the previous page but the map is called δ in (5); this is a notational slip.

Universality of G → I_G 'after base change' holds for SL2 and GL2, and more generally for simply connected Chevalley groups over Z by Steinberg. For a general reductive group over an arbitrary base, formation of G//G commutes with flat base change, but with arbitrary base change only up to universal homeomorphism (Seshadri). The claim is stated without restriction to the cases at hand.

The claim that equal images in I_G suffice for fppf-local conjugacy of regular sections over a general base needs smoothness of the regular centralizer and of the Chevalley map on G^reg. This is true, but it is a relative strengthening of Steinberg's field-theoretic result, asserted here without proof.

ideas.what: Commutator map α ↦ [α,ρ] factors through a monomorphism G/Centr(ρ) ↪ G; its image is the set of ξ with ξρ locally conjugate to ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Orbit map / commutator fibres; conjugacy class of ρ translated by ρ^{-1}

ideas.what: Abelianization obstruction δ(ξ)=1 as a necessary condition for being a commutator.
ideas.modern_name: Commutator lies in the derived subgroup / kernel of det

ideas.what: Scheme of invariants I_G as the universal conjugation-invariant map from G to schemes, the 'representable envelope' of the sheaf of conjugacy classes, compatible with base change.
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint quotient / Chevalley–Steinberg map G → G//G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chevalley, Steinberg (1965), Seshadri for base change
ideas.where_published: SGA3 treats related material; not sure it is stated in this form

ideas.what: Regular (or semisimple) sections with the same image in I_G are locally (fppf) conjugate; for SL2 and GL2, regular means nowhere central.
ideas.modern_name: Steinberg's theorem on regular elements; relative version via the regular centralizer (cf. Ngô, Bouthier)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: commutator map orbits plus the Steinberg/Chevalley adjoint quotient, applied to SL2/GL2 over Z. It is a working step in the loop-equation notes, with no new result or unexplored connection beyond the well-known trace description.
transcription_corrections: 'nécessaire et suffisante, topologiquement [?]' should read 'nécessaire et suffisante, tautologiquement, puisque ...'
The insertion '(sur A, et compris [?] et chgt de base)' likely reads '(sur A, et universellement / y compris après chgt de base)'.
Condition (4) on the previous page uses Δ, but this page writes δ.
